record.what_it_does: Payments, billing, invoicing, payouts and financial infrastructure platform with a broad REST API.
record.auth_notes: The API takes API keys via HTTP Basic Auth (key as username) or an Authorization: Bearer header. Key types are secret sk_, restricted rk_ (RAK), organisation sk_org_, and agent-tagged RAKs that are subject to approval rules. Workload Identity Federation exchanges a cloud identity token for a Stripe access token that lasts 1 hour. For per-user access, Stripe Apps OAuth 2.0 (marketplace.stripe.com/oauth/v2/authorize) issues access tokens that expire after 1 hour and refresh tokens that last 1 year and roll on each exchange. Stripe Apps can also use RAK-install authentication. Connect OAuth (connect.stripe.com/oauth) still exists, but Stripe's publish guide says the Connect authentication method is deprecated in favour of Stripe Apps OAuth, and the Connect token response marks access_token and refresh_token as deprecated. A multi-user toolkit should use Stripe Apps OAuth.
record.access_notes: A free Stripe account gives sandbox/test keys right away, and live keys for your own account need no review. OAuth apps can be tested with a limited number of accounts through External test links. Public distribution of an OAuth Stripe App requires an activated account, a Marketplace listing and app review (about 4 business days, with re-review on every change). Public OAuth install links don't work until the app is published. Stripe has deprecated Connect OAuth as the alternative route.
record.api_breadth_notes: Covers customers, charges, PaymentIntents, SetupIntents, Checkout, invoices, subscriptions, products and prices, coupons, payment links, disputes, refunds, payouts, balance, Issuing, Tax, Radar, Connect, webhook endpoints and event destinations, and v2 money-management (Treasury) endpoints. The MCP page alone lists about 170 supported API methods, a subset of the full API. Both v1 and v2 APIs exist. A public OpenAPI spec is published at github.com/stripe/openapi.
record.mcp_notes: https://mcp.stripe.com (official, remote). Supports OAuth (refresh tokens expire after 14 days) or agent API keys sent as a Bearer token. Tools include stripe_api_search, stripe_api_details, stripe_api_read, stripe_api_write, get_stripe_account_info, stripe_analytics, Treasury tools and search_stripe_documentation. From 11 January 2027 it will reject full-access secret keys and non-agent restricted keys. OAuth isn't supported when acting on connected accounts; use an agent key with the Stripe-Account header instead.
record.blocker_notes: Per-user OAuth for public distribution needs a public Stripe App, which requires an activated account and passing Marketplace app review (about 4 business days, with re-review on changes). Connect OAuth is not a clean alternative because Stripe calls it deprecated. API keys (preferably restricted or agent keys) work immediately with no review, so an API-key toolkit can ship today.

evidence.quote: Stripe’s MCP server supports two authentication methods:
OAuth refresh tokens expire after 14 days
The Stripe API authenticates requests using HTTP Basic Auth. Provide your API key as the basic auth username value.
If you need to authenticate using bearer auth (for example, for a cross-origin request), use -H "Authorization: Bearer <<YOUR_SECRET_KEY>>"
Access tokens expire in 1 hour, and refresh tokens expire after 1 year.
The public OAuth install links don’t work until the app is published.
Submit your app for review (then wait 4 business days)
Stripe deprecated the Connect Stripe authentication method, so use this OAuth method instead.
This repository contains OpenAPI specifications for Stripe's API.
The Stripe MCP server exposes multiple APIs that you can call with the `stripe_api_read` and `stripe_api_write` tools.
After you register a webhook endpoint, Stripe pushes real-time data to it when events happen in your Stripe account.
A sandbox is an isolated test environment that allows you to test Stripe functionality in your account without affecting your live integration.
